title: Alive or Not Alive?
introductionText:
Biology
Alive or Not Alive?
The Big Idea: Living things grow, need food and water, breathe, move by themselves, feel the world around them, and make new living
things like themselves. Non‑living things never do any of this.
Say It Like This
Read aloud
"A car moves, doesn't it? But does a car ever get hungry? Does a car ever grow bigger? Does a baby car ever come out of a big car? No! So a
car is not alive. Now think about you. You eat. You drink. You breathe. You grow taller every year. You are alive! And a tree is alive too — it
drinks water, it grows taller, and it makes seeds that become baby trees."
Watch Out For
Two mistakes almost every child makes
1. "It moves, so it is alive." Keep pointing at the car, the clock, the ceiling fan, the river. They all move, and none of them is alive. Moving is
not enough.
2. "Plants are not alive because they don't walk." Show him the bean you are growing in Unit 2. It got taller. It drank the water. It is alive.
Try It at Home
The house hunt — 10 minutes
Walk slowly through the house together. Point at things one by one: a chair, the cat, a plant, a mug, grandmother, the television, a fly on
the window. For each one ask the same three questions: "Does it grow? Does it need food? Can it make babies?" If the answer is yes to all
three, it is alive. Make two lists on one sheet of paper: Alive and Not Alive.
ALIVE NOT ALIVE
they grow, feed, breathe and make babies a car moves, but it never grows or eats
Moving is not enough. Ask the three questions: does it grow, feed and make babies?
More examples to talk about
Alive: the cat on the stairs, a mosquito, the mint growing on the balcony, a fish in a bowl, the bread mould in the kitchen, grandmother, a
date palm.
Not alive: a wooden spoon, a cloud, the fridge, a doll, a stone, a car, water in a glass.
The tricky ones — ask him to think hard: a cloud moves but is not alive. A wooden chair was once part of a living tree, but the chair itself is
not alive. An egg is alive — there is a baby chick growing inside.
Key Words
alive not alive living thing grow breathe food

sourceQuestions.sourceText:
Draw a circle around the things that are alive:
giraffe car tree chair human mug plant lizard
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: Alive: giraffe, tree, human, plant, lizard. Not alive: car, chair, mug.

sourceQuestions.sourceText:
Complete the sentences about a pet bird. Use these words: moves, eats, breathes, grown
a) The bird around his cage.
b) The bird when he is hungry.
c) The bird through two holes in his beak.
d) The bird was a baby. Now he has bigger.
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: a) moves b) eats c) breathes d) grown

sourceQuestions.sourceText:
Is a kettle alive? Circle one: YES / NO
Say why:
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: No. A kettle does not grow, does not need food, and cannot make new kettles. It only moves when a person moves it.

sourceQuestions.sourceText: Write two things a dandelion plant does that show it is alive.
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: Any two of: it grows; it needs water and food; it makes new dandelion plants (seeds); it makes its own food from sunlight.

sourceQuestions.sourceText: True or false? "Everything that moves is alive." TRUE / FALSE
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: FALSE. A car, a clock and a river all move and none of them is alive.

sourceQuestions.sourceText: Draw one living thing and one non‑living thing that you can see in your room right now. Write their names underneath.
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: Child's own drawing. Living: a person, a pet, a plant, an insect. Non‑living: a chair, a toy, a book, a lamp.

sourceQuestions.sourceText: Write two things a cat does that show it is alive.
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: Any two: it grows; it eats and drinks; it breathes; it moves by itself; it feels things; it can have kittens.

sourceQuestions.sourceText:
Sort these into the right list: cloud, worm, bread, mint plant, doll, fly
Alive Not alive
sourceQuestions.answerKeyText: Alive: worm, mint plant, fly. Not alive: cloud, bread, doll. (Bread was made from wheat that was alive, but the bread itself is not.)

sourceQuestions.sourceText: Which one of these is alive? ( a car ) ( a tree ) ( a chair )
All living things need food and ( water ) ( toys ) ( paper )
Which is not a sign of being alive? ( growing ) ( eating ) ( being made in a factory )
A baby bird will one day ( stay the same size ) ( grow bigger ) ( get smaller )
